note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God, Sheol and death are not pictured as figures, Job and his friends are not portrayed as biblical people but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown (the spitting of verse 6 is shown as public scorn).
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Job's spirit is broken and his days are used up; the grave is all that is left for him, and only mockers are round him.
ideas: A gaunt grey-haired man sits slumped at a bare kitchen table at night beside an hourglass whose sand has all run out
A worn man sits alone on a bench among weathered headstones at dusk, utterly spent
A candle's last smoke curls up from a wick just snuffed out in a dark room
A man sits on the edge of a hospital bed in a dim ward, his head bowed
A man sits on a park bench with his head in his hands while young men nearby point and laugh
A burnt-out match lies curled and black on a table
A man stares at a fire in the hearth that has burned down to grey ash
A hollow-eyed face in a cracked mirror
A wilted flower in a glass with its petals fallen round it
The last leaf falls from a bare tree in grey weather

sections.meaning: No friend will stand surety for him, so Job asks God himself to put down the pledge for him and clasp his hand.
ideas: A worn man holds out his open hand for a handshake while the three men facing him keep their arms folded
On a bright hillside a worn man stretches his open hand up toward the sky while three men walk away down the hill behind him
A man sits at a bank desk with a paper waiting for a co-signer, the chair beside him empty
Two hands meet in a firm handshake that seals a promise
A man stands alone at a courtroom rail and no one steps forward to speak for him
A child in a crowd reaches up for a hand to hold
A man in the rain holds out his hand to friends who walk away with their backs turned
A man holds out an empty open palm across a table where no one sits
A friend takes an envelope of money in a dim stairwell while pointing out another friend's door
A man waits at a closed door with his hand raised to knock

sections.meaning: He has become a byword that people sneer at, his eyes dim with grief and his body worn down to a shadow.
ideas: A gaunt hollow-eyed man walks down a town street while neighbours in doorways whisper and point at him
Young people stand round a gaunt man laughing and filming him on their phones
A thin man sits by a window, his frail shadow stretched long on the wall
Close view of an old man's tired eyes, red and clouded with tears
People turn their backs one by one as a ragged man passes
A coat hangs loose on a man who has grown very thin
A man sits alone at a cafe while the other tables stare and mutter
A gaunt face looks into a mirror at a body grown thin
Children copy a sick man's slow walk behind his back
A man's thin shadow on a pavement is all we see of him

sections.meaning: Good people are shocked at such suffering, yet the righteous keep to their way, and the one with clean hands only grows stronger.
ideas: A lone walker in driving rain keeps steadily up a straight mountain path without turning aside
Clean strong hands grip a rock hold firmly and pull the climber higher
A tree bent by a storm wind with its roots holding firm
A farmer keeps ploughing a straight furrow as storm clouds gather
A lighthouse stands firm while waves break over it
Washed hands take hold of a heavy rope and pull
A hiker keeps climbing the trail while others turn back down
A straight line of footprints across deep snow
A runner keeps going in the rain after the others have stopped
Neighbours watch shocked from a porch while a man walks on through the storm

sections.meaning: His friends bring no wisdom: his days are over and his heart's plans broken off, yet they tell him light is near while it is dark.
ideas: A half-built house stands abandoned in an overgrown field, tools left where they fell
At night a cheerful friend points at a pitch-black horizon while the grieving man sits in the dark
An unfinished wooden boat sits in a dusty shed with the tools laid down
A bridge built halfway across a river and stopped
A kite string snapped, the kite falling away
Someone throws open the curtains onto a pitch-black night as if it were morning
A friend switches on a small desk lamp at midnight and points to it like the sun
An unfinished painting on an easel covered in dust
A garden half dug and left, the spade still standing in the earth
Friends talk brightly round a man who stares into the dark

sections.meaning: If the grave is all he can hope for, he must make his home and his bed in the dark and call the pit and the worm his family.
ideas: A neatly made bed stands alone in a pitch-dark stone cellar, faint light from the stairs far above
A gaunt man lies awake on a bed in a bare dark room staring at the ceiling
A man walks down stone stairs into darkness carrying a pillow
A blanket and pillow laid out on bare earth in a dark hollow
A dark empty house with every piece of furniture covered in sheets
Dead leaves blow through the open door of an empty house
A doormat laid before a doorway that opens onto blackness
A family photograph laid face down on a dusty table
A house half sunk into mud
A lamp going out in an underground room

sections.meaning: Then where is his hope, and who can see it? It will go down with him into the dust.
ideas: An old man holds up a lantern, searching across a vast dark empty plain at night
Worn stone steps lead down to an iron-barred gate standing open on darkness, dust thick on the steps
A man sifts through dust with his hands looking for something lost
A tiny light far down at the bottom of a deep well
A man searches with a torch in thick night fog
Footprints in the dust that lead down a slope and stop
A man scans a black horizon at night and sees nothing
A ring lying half buried in grey dust
Dust running out between an old man's fingers
A dry seed lying on dust

candidates.prompt: Late at night in a bare, dim kitchen, a gaunt grey-haired man in a plain shirt sits slumped at a wooden table, his shoulders fallen and his eyes empty, utterly worn out. On the table in front of him stands a large hourglass in which every grain of sand has already run down into the bottom; the top glass is completely empty. One small lamp gives the only light.

At grey dusk in a quiet old cemetery, a gaunt grey-haired man in a plain coat sits alone, slumped on a wooden bench among rows of weathered, moss-covered headstones, his head bowed and his hands hanging loose between his knees, utterly spent. The headstones are plain and worn smooth, with nothing carved on them.

In a plain living room, a worn grey-haired man in an old cardigan stands holding out his open right hand for a handshake, his face pleading. Facing him stand three well-dressed men with their arms folded tightly, leaning back, not one of them reaching to take his hand. His outstretched empty hand is in the middle of the frame, clear and sharp.

On an open grassy hillside under a wide bright sky with white clouds, a worn grey-haired man in a plain shirt, seen from behind, stretches one open hand up and out toward the bright sky, as if waiting for someone above to take hold of it. Far behind him, down the hill, three men walk away with their backs turned.

On a narrow present-day town street in daylight, a gaunt, hollow-eyed man in a worn coat walks alone with his head down, thin and frail as a shadow. On both sides neighbours stand in doorways and at windows, whispering behind their hands, smirking and pointing at him as he passes.

In a present-day town square, a gaunt, hollow-eyed man in a worn coat sits hunched on the edge of a stone fountain, thin and frail. A ring of young people stand round him laughing, pointing at him and holding up their phones to film him, the phone screens turned away from us.

In driving rain on a bare mountainside, a man in a plain rain jacket walks steadily up a narrow, straight path, head lowered into the weather, keeping to the path without turning aside. The path runs on ahead of him up the slope into the grey storm light.

Close view of a pair of clean, strong hands gripping a rough rock hold firmly on a steep wet cliff face, a climber pulling himself higher, knuckles tight, rain on the rock around the hands, a safety rope running beside them.

A half-built wooden house stands abandoned in an overgrown field: its bare timber frame has walls only part of the way up and the roof unfinished and open to the sky. A ladder and a few tools lie where they were dropped, and tall weeds and grass have grown up through the floor. Overcast afternoon light.

At night in a dark field, a grieving man sits slumped on a low stone wall. Beside him a cheerful friend in a jacket smiles broadly and points eagerly at the pitch-black horizon, where there is no sign of light at all; the whole sky is black. Only a faint glow from a distant house window lets us see the two of them.

A narrow bed, neatly made with a pillow and a blanket, stands alone in a bare stone cellar deep underground, in near darkness. A single faint shaft of grey light falls from a stairway high above, just enough to show the bed; everything else is black.

Late at night a gaunt man lies on his back on a bed in a bare, dark, empty room, eyes open, staring up at the ceiling. There is nothing else in the room, only deep darkness all round and a faint grey glow from a window falling across his face.

At night on a vast, dark, empty plain, an old man in a plain coat stands holding a lantern up high, peering out into the blackness, searching for something he cannot find. The small circle of lantern light shows only bare dust and stones around his feet; beyond it is darkness all the way to the horizon.

Worn stone steps lead down into darkness, ending at an old iron-barred gate standing open at the bottom, with only blackness beyond it. Fine grey dust lies thick on the steps. Dim grey light falls from above.
